newsitem.title: UK: Palladium leads strength in London precious metals.
newsitem.headline: Palladium leads strength in London precious metals.

text.p: Palladium held the spotlight
in precious metals on Tuesday as it leapt higher on new delays expected in Russian supplies and gold and silver were firm.
Dealers said the price of the rare metal, mainly used in
autocatalysts and electronics, could spike up toward $160.00 an ounce from $154.50/$155.50 on Tuesday, already up $2.50.
Palladium firmed after a Russian trade official said
there would be no PGM shipments in April and possibly in May.
"It scuppered any plans of getting palladium into
Japan... even if they did start re-supplying there would be a lot of (backlog of) demand in Japan," said one London dealer.
"Palladium is always going to look good for a bet on the
upside anyway," he added.
Bullion crawled higher but stayed within a well-worn
range. It looked secure above $348.00 but dealers were sceptical of any steep gains with $350.00-$351.00 being a resistance area.
Gold fixed at $349.10 versus $349.00 on Monday and
against New York's close of $348.00/$348.50.
"I can't see gold going too much higher. Even if it does
go through $350.00 there would be a lot of selling," one dealer said, adding that a grim chart picture and the strength of the dollar against the yen and mark was likely to cap further gains.
Bullion was indicated at $349.00/$349.50 at 1035 GMT.
Karen Jones, analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston said the market was due for a bounce to the top of its range at $350.00 after underlying support levels survived downside tests.
But she described the market as "neutral" for the moment.
Consolidation held silver above $4.80 at $4.82/$4.84 but, as in gold, a big follow-through on the upside looked doubtful although chartwise $4.90 was possible.
"There may be a bit of room on the upside but over next week or so it may try lower again," said the London-based dealer.
Jones meanwhile pegged first resistance at $4.84. Silver had ended Monday's trading at $4.79/$4.81 an ounce.
The strength of palladium kept platinum firm and the price was unchanged at $366.50/$367.50 on Tuesday morning. Some analysts saw scope for piercing resistance at $375.00.
In palladium, Swiss buyers were spearheading the demand and borrowing, although speculative interest was also cited.
Lease rates were sharply higher with one month palladium quoted at six percent in Tokyo, from around 2-2.5 percent a week ago, dealers said. "That's unheard of," said one.
-- Clelia Oziel London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
